label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Strained
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend substantial time on social media (averaging nearly 4 hours daily, with many exceeding 5 hours) and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Across all three psychological measures—loneliness (UCLA-8), depression (PHQ-9), and anxiety (GAD-7)—their scores are notably higher than typical respondents, with anxiety symptoms being particularly pronounced. The combination of heavy social-media engagement and co-occurring emotional distress characterizes this sizable cluster of 140 respondents.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily social-media use exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Heavy daily social-media consumption averaging approximately 3.9 hours with a substantial proportion exceeding 5 hours
Elevated loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ~1.78) indicating persistent feelings of social disconnection
Moderate-to-high depressive symptom burden (PHQ-9 mean ~1.81)
Notably high anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 mean ~2.27), the most pronounced psychological indicator in this profile
Co-occurrence of all three distress dimensions alongside intensive digital social engagement
tone: Concerned and empathetic, grounded in observed data patterns

label: Well-Adjusted Light-Use Graduate Male
summary: This profile represents male respondents with graduate-level education or above who report notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. Their daily social media use is relatively light, averaging roughly 2.8 hours (within the 1–3 hour bracket). Across all psychological well-being indicators, this group scores well below scale midpoints, suggesting generally positive mental health and moderate digital engagement.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily social media use
behavior_markers: Light daily social media consumption averaging approximately 2.8 hours
Very low loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.78, well below scale midpoint)
Minimal depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.27)
Near-floor anxiety levels (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.03)
Pattern consistent with balanced digital habits and strong psychosocial functioning

label: Lonely but Low-Distress Heavy Social-Media User
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend nearly 5 hours per day on social media and report elevated loneliness, yet exhibit comparatively lower levels of depressive and anxiety symptoms. Despite heavy digital engagement, their psychological distress remains below average on clinical screening measures, suggesting that their social-media use coexists with higher perceived social isolation without translating into pronounced mood or anxiety difficulties.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, 3–5 hours of daily social-media use
behavior_markers: Heavy daily social-media consumption averaging approximately 4.9 hours
Elevated loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.30) indicating moderate perceived social isolation
Below-average depressive symptom levels (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.90)
Below-average anxiety symptom levels (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.85)
Disconnect between high online engagement and subjective feelings of loneliness
tone: Socially connected online yet personally isolated; functionally stable with an undercurrent of unmet relational needs

label: Well-Adjusted Graduate Male with Light Social-Media Use
summary: This profile represents a group of 217 respondents characterized by notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms, combined with relatively light daily social-media use averaging roughly 1.6 hours. Their mean scores on the UCLA-8 loneliness scale (1.22), PHQ-9 depression scale (0.82), and GAD-7 anxiety scale (0.90) all fall well below clinical concern thresholds, suggesting generally positive psychological well-being. These individuals tend to be highly educated males who maintain a moderate and controlled relationship with social media.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, reporting 1–3 hours of daily social-media use
behavior_markers: Light daily social-media use averaging approximately 1.6 hours
Loneliness scores well below scale midpoints (UCLA-8 mean: 1.22)
Minimal depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean: 0.82)
Low anxiety symptom levels (GAD-7 mean: 0.90)
Social-media engagement kept within a moderate 1–3 hour daily window
